ai.lead: How can AI learn from experience and preserve acquired capabilities? Bavaria AeroTech is researching an architecture intended to connect new knowledge with prior experience. The goal is to enable learning and processing on a device or within dedicated infrastructure.
ai.why: Autonomous systems encounter changing situations. A useful architecture must connect new knowledge with existing knowledge while retaining acquired capabilities. How to achieve this reliably remains an open research question.
ai.method: The approach studies digital neuron-like elements with internal states. They receive signals, pass them on and influence one another. Experience is intended to change connections and link new knowledge to what was previously learned. Learning, memory and behaviour are intended to work together.
ai.sovereignty: The project aims for systems whose processing and adaptation can take place on a device or within dedicated infrastructure. Organizations should be able to understand and control the architecture, data and changes. A permanent connection to an external service should not be required.
ai.applications: Possible fields include local computers, industrial systems and robotics, including unmanned platforms where local processing can matter when connectivity is limited. These are potential areas for future research.
ai.next: SOUVERÄN-AI is at the research and concept stage. Planned steps include testing whether individual elements can store and reproduce experience, studying how they work together, then building an integrated experimental architecture for evaluation on available computing platforms.
ai.criteria: Evaluation should consider retention of acquired capabilities, memory needs, computing effort, energy use and traceability of changes. Whether the architecture can meet these aims remains to be investigated.
ai.finance: Funding would support building the experimental architecture and testing its underlying principles. A discussion can define the next research step and possible cooperation.
ai.whyDetail: The question becomes especially clear when tasks, environments or available information change. An architecture intended to learn from experience must take in new observations and relate them to what it has already learned. At the same time, a new adaptation should not automatically mean losing a capability acquired earlier. How both goals can be pursued within one structure and assessed reliably is one of the project’s central open questions. The work addresses this specific question and does not make a blanket claim to replace other methods.
ai.methodDetail: In the concept, an element is not limited to a fixed input and output. Its internal state is intended to influence how it responds to new signals. Elements can pass information to one another and form a larger structure together. As that structure processes experience, changes to one element are intended to affect its later responses. This could create a connection between retained experience and current behaviour. Whether the elements can work together stably, how information is retained and how a targeted adaptation can be achieved all require experimental investigation.
ai.sovereigntyDetail: Operation on a device or within controlled infrastructure can give organisations more influence over where data is processed and which changes enter a system. This requires the structure, data flows and adaptation steps to be traceable. Local processing alone does not guarantee security or control; it is one possible technical component whose limits must also be examined. SOUVERÄN-AI investigates whether learning and processing can be designed to work without a continuously available external platform.
ai.applicationsDetail: For local computers, research would examine whether the architecture can operate within limited memory and computing resources. In industrial systems, traceable adaptation and controllable behaviour would matter. Civilian robotics and uncrewed platforms raise the additional question of how a system might respond to changing conditions and temporarily limited connectivity. These are possible future areas of investigation, not announced products or deployment-ready applications. Their selection and scope depend on whether the foundational experiments produce robust findings.
ai.stepOne: First, individual digital elements are to be examined to see whether they can take in and retain experience and later draw on it in relevant situations.
ai.stepTwo: Next, the interaction of several elements is to be assessed: whether information is retained across the overall structure and whether changes in one place have traceable effects.
ai.stepThree: Only then would an integrated experimental architecture be assembled and assessed on available computing platforms. This sequence describes the next research path, not milestones already completed.
ai.nextDetail: Each step needs suitable, traceable experiments. The assessment should record whether capabilities remain after new adaptations, how much memory and computing power are required, and how energy demand develops. It must also be possible to see which change led to which behaviour. Comparing these criteria can show where the architecture works, where it reaches limits and which questions remain open.
ai.financeDetail: Research funding would enable the development of a limited experimental architecture and its assessment on available platforms. An initial discussion can clarify the scope of a suitable work package, potential research partners and appropriate test conditions. The concrete design depends on the outcome of those discussions and on available resources.
